variables.name: STUDYID
variables.label: Study Identifier
variables.description: Unique identifier for a study.

variables.name: DOMAIN
variables.label: Domain Abbreviation
variables.description: Two-character abbreviation for the domain.

variables.name: USUBJID
variables.label: Unique Subject Identifier
variables.description: Identifier used to uniquely identify a subject across all studies for all applications or submissions involving the product.

variables.name: AGSEQ
variables.label: Sequence Number
variables.description: Sequence number given to ensure uniqueness of subject records within a domain. May be any valid number.

variables.name: AGGRPID
variables.label: Group ID
variables.description: Used to tie together a block of related records in a single domain for a subject.

variables.name: AGSPID
variables.label: Sponsor-Defined Identifier
variables.description: Sponsor-defined reference number. May be preprinted on the CRF as an explicit line identifier or defined in the sponsor's operational database. Example: Line number from the procedure or test page.

variables.name: AGLNKID
variables.label: Link ID
variables.description: Identifier used to link related records across domains.This may be a one-to-one or a one-to-many relationship.

variables.name: AGLNKGRP
variables.label: Link Group ID
variables.description: Identifier used to link related records across domains.This will usually be a many-to-one relationship.

variables.name: AGTRT
variables.label: Reported Agent Name
variables.description: Verbatim medication name that is either preprinted or collected on a CRF.

variables.name: AGMODIFY
variables.label: Modified Reported Name
variables.description: If AGTRT is modified to facilitate coding, then AGMODIFY will contain the modified text.

variables.name: AGDECOD
variables.label: Standardized Agent Name
variables.description: Standardized or dictionary-derived text description of AGTRT or AGMODIFY. Equivalent to the generic medication name in WHO Drug. The sponsor is expected to provide the dictionary name and version used to map the terms utilizing the external codelist element in the Define-XML document. If an intervention term does not have a decode value in the dictionary, then AGDECOD will be left blank.

variables.name: AGCAT
variables.label: Category for Agent
variables.description: Used to define a category of agent. Examples: "CHALLENGE AGENT", "PET TRACER".

variables.name: AGSCAT
variables.label: Subcategory for Agent
variables.description: Further categorization of agent.

variables.name: AGPRESP
variables.label: AG Pre-Specified
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66742
variables.description: Used to indicate whether ("Y"/null) information about the use of a specific agent was solicited on the CRF.

variables.name: AGOCCUR
variables.label: AG Occurrence
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66742
variables.description: When the use of specific agent is solicited, AGOCCUR is used to indicate whether ("Y"/"N") use of the agent occurred. Values are null for agents not specifically solicited.

variables.name: AGSTAT
variables.label: Completion Status
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66789
variables.description: Used to indicate that a question about a prespecified agent was not answered. Should be null or have a value of "NOT DONE".

variables.name: AGREASND
variables.label: Reason Procedure Agent Not Collected
variables.description: Describes the reason a response to a question about the occurrence of a procedure agent was not collected. Used in conjunction with AGSTAT when value is "NOT DONE".

variables.name: AGCLAS
variables.label: Agent Class
variables.description: Drug class. May be obtained from coding. When coding to a single class, populate with class value. If using a dictionary and coding to multiple classes, follow guidance in Section 4.2.8.3, Multiple Values for a Non-result Qualifier Variable, or omit AGCLAS.

variables.name: AGCLASCD
variables.label: Agent Class Code
variables.description: Class code corresponding to AGCLAS. Drug class. May be obtained from coding. When coding to a single class, populate with class code. If using a dictionary and coding to multiple classes, follow guidance in Section 4.2.8.3, Multiple Values for a Non-result Qualifier Variable, or omit AGCLASCD.

variables.name: AGDOSE
variables.label: Dose per Administration
variables.description: Amount of AGTRT taken.

variables.name: AGDOSTXT
variables.label: Dose Description
variables.description: Dosing amounts or a range of dosing information collected in text form. Units may be stored in AGDOSU. Examples: "200-400", "15-20".

variables.name: AGDOSU
variables.label: Dose Units
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C71620
variables.description: Units for AGDOSE and AGDOSTXT. Examples: "ng", "mg", "mg/kg".

variables.name: AGDOSFRM
variables.label: Dose Form
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66726
variables.description: Dose form for AGTRT. Examples: "TABLET", "AEROSOL".

variables.name: AGDOSFRQ
variables.label: Dosing Frequency per Interval
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C71113
variables.description: Usually expressed as the number of repeated administrations of AGDOSE within a specific time period. Example: "ONCE".

variables.name: AGROUTE
variables.label: Route of Administration
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66729
variables.description: Route of administration for AGTRT. Example: "ORAL".

variables.name: VISITNUM
variables.label: Visit Number
variables.description: 1. Clinical encounter number. \n 2. Numeric version of VISIT, used for sorting.

variables.name: VISIT
variables.label: Visit Name
variables.description: 1. Protocol-defined description of clinical encounter. \n 2. May be used in addition to VISITNUM and/or VISITDY.

variables.name: VISITDY
variables.label: Planned Study Day of Visit
variables.description: Planned study day of the visit based upon RFSTDTC in Demographics.

variables.name: TAETORD
variables.label: Planned Order of Element within Arm
variables.description: Number that gives the planned order of the element within the arm for the element in which the agent administration started.

variables.name: EPOCH
variables.label: Epoch
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C99079
variables.description: Epoch associated with the start date/time of the agent administration started.

variables.name: AGSTDTC
variables.label: Start Date/Time of Agent
variables.description: The date/time when administration of the treatment indicated by AGTRT and the dosing variables began.

variables.name: AGENDTC
variables.label: End Date/Time of Agent
variables.description: The date/time when administration of the treatment indicated by AGTRT and the dosing variables ended.

variables.name: AGSTDY
variables.label: Study Day of Start of Agent
variables.description: Study day of start of agent relative to the sponsor-defined RFSTDTC.

variables.name: AGENDY
variables.label: Study Day of End of Agent
variables.description: Study day of end of agent relative to the sponsor-defined RFSTDTC.

variables.name: AGDUR
variables.label: Duration of Agent
variables.description: Collected duration for an agent episode. Used only if collected on the CRF and not derived from start and end date/times.

variables.name: AGSTRF
variables.label: Start Relative to Reference Period
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66728
variables.description: Describes the start of the agent relative to sponsor-defined reference period. The sponsor-defined reference period is a continuous period of time defined by a discrete starting point and a discrete ending point (represented by RFSTDTC and RFENDTC in Demographics). If information such as "PRIOR", "ONGOING", or "CONTINUING" was collected, this information may be translated into AGSTRF. \n Not all values of the codelist are allowable for this variable. See Section 4.4.7, Use of Relative Timing Variables.

variables.name: AGENRF
variables.label: End Relative to Reference Period
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66728
variables.description: Describes the end of the agent relative to the sponsor-defined reference period. The sponsor-defined reference period is a continuous period of time defined by a discrete starting point and a discrete ending point (represented by RFSTDTC and RFENDTC in Demographics). If information such as "PRIOR", "ONGOING", or "CONTINUING" was collected, this information may be translated into AGENRF. \n Not all values of the codelist are allowable for this variable. See Section 4.4.7, Use of Relative Timing Variables.

variables.name: AGSTRTPT
variables.label: Start Relative to Reference Time Point
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66728
variables.description: Identifies the start of the agent as being before or after the sponsor-defined reference time point defined by variable AGSTTPT. \n Not all values of the codelist are allowable for this variable. See Section 4.4.7, Use of Relative Timing Variables.

variables.name: AGSTTPT
variables.label: Start Reference Time Point
variables.description: Description or date/time in ISO 8601 character format of the reference point referred to by AGSTRTPT. Examples: "2003-12-15", "VISIT 1".

variables.name: AGENRTPT
variables.label: End Relative to Reference Time Point
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66728
variables.description: Identifies the end of the agent as being before or after the reference time point defined by variable AGENTPT. Identifies the end of the agent as being before or after the sponsor-defined reference time point defined by variable AGENTPT. \n Not all values of the codelist are allowable for this variable. See Section 4.4.7, Use of Relative Timing Variables.

variables.name: AGENTPT
variables.label: End Reference Time Point
variables.description: Description or date/time in ISO 8601 character format of the reference point referred to by AGENRTPT. Examples: "2003-12-25", "VISIT 2".
